## 2026-11-13T19:45Z Creative render completes end to end for the first time

Run `43483476413` at `49703e58` is the first run where the full creative path passed: reference analysis, authoring, and **Render and repair creative candidates** all report success. The visual-gate retry (`fb71995a`) and the analyzer fixes are working.

The preview build then rejected the candidate, correctly:

- `decision: reject`, `promotionReady: false`
- Hard failure: `contrast fail: / desktop default ... a:nth-of-type(2) text "0598020802" (1.000; required 4.5); foreground #14201d, background variable; overlapping non-ancestor paint requires rendered review, resolved from rendered pixels`
- Plus at least one `contrast unresolved` focus finding

That is a real defect in the authored candidate (a dark ink link over an unmeasured backdrop in the hero), not a template bug. With the preview policy now at one candidate and one repair cycle there is no second candidate to select, so the single defect rejects the render and the run fails before the pack fallback can deploy.

This is the trade the one-candidate policy makes, and it needs a decision: either raise the repair-cycle bound for preview, or let a near-miss candidate deliver with warnings when the only failure is an advisory contrast class that the local design repair can fix after delivery.

### Root cause of the remaining reject

The failing selector sits inside `astro-island`, the hydrated client boundary. `verify-rendered-revision` audits the built page including hydrated islands, while the creative gate judges rendered screenshots. A link inside a hydrated island can therefore pass the creative gate and still fail the final whole-page contrast audit, which is what happened: the candidate's hero phone link measured 1.000 against an unmeasured backdrop.

`contrast fail` stays hard (a 1.000 ratio means invisible text, which is critical accessibility), while `contrast unresolved` is already advisory. The correct fix is to make the creative gate audit the hydrated page rather than only screenshots, not to downgrade the check.

**Retracted at 21:52Z.** The creative gate already audits the built page through the same
`rendered-contrast.mjs`, so there was no hydrated-island scope gap. The 1.000 was the element's
own border sampled as backdrop; see the 21:52Z entry below.

## 2026-11-13T21:52Z The 1.000 contrast failures were the element's own border

Worktree `.worktrees/launchloom-island-contrast`, branch `codex/launchloom-island-contrast`.

Work OS ledger: not created. The canonical VPS copy is unreachable from this machine
(`ssh -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine dev@72.62.5.190` times out on port 22, ICMP 100% loss,
IPv6 `2a02:4780:f:eba3::1` reports network unreachable, retried over roughly an hour).
Recording the work here until the ledger is reachable, then creating the task retroactively.

### Root cause

The creative preview build rejected intake 146 on twelve `contrast fail` lines, six of them
exactly `1.000` with two different foregrounds and six at `1.180`. Reproduced on the real built
page, then in a four-element fixture:

- `0598020802` default: `1.000 #14201d`. The link is `.ll-btn-quiet` with
  `background:#e8eee5; color:#14201d; border:1px solid #14201d`. `resolveRenderedBackdrop`
  captures the element box and measures the worst pixel in it. The 1px border is the same
  colour as the text, so the "backdrop" evaluated equal to the foreground and the ratio
  collapsed to exactly 1.000. The real contrast is 13.2:1.
- `0598020802` hover: `1.000 #e8eee5`, same mechanism inverted (text becomes the pale surface
  colour while the dark fill and border stay).
- `Call now` hover: `1.180 #ffffff`. The element screenshot's clip includes a sliver of the
  surrounding `#e8eee5` panel at the fractional element edge, and white against that panel is
  1.180. The real contrast against the `#027262` hover fill is 5.36:1.

The same element without the border measured 14.187 and the button without the edge sliver
measured 5.856, which isolates the cause. This is not a hydrated-island scope gap: the creative
gate already audits the built page through the same `rendered-contrast.mjs`.

### Fixes

- `scripts/rendered-contrast.mjs`: `analyzePixelBackdrop` gains an edge `inset`, and
  `resolveRenderedBackdrop` re-measures without the element's own painted edge and keeps the
  **better** ratio. Excluding the edge can only rescue a failure, never invent one, so the
  change cannot weaken a genuine finding. A focus ring keeps its own perimeter band. Capture
  errors now log under `LL_CONTRAST_DEBUG=1` instead of vanishing.
- `templates/client-site/src/lib/color-policy.mjs`: the `focus` ring is proved against the
  darkest recurring light band (and lightest dark band), not only its own surface.
- `templates/client-site/src/layouts/SiteLayout.astro`: expose `--ll-focus` on the body. It was
  only emitted inside `[data-ll-surface]` scopes, so platform chrome such as the quick-answers
  launcher fell back to its own hardcoded `#439d8b` ring and measured 2.647:1 against a light
  band. It is now `#348f7e` at 3.024:1 worst case.

### Verification

- Real built page for intake 146 (client repo `review/initial`, `PUBLIC_REVIEW_MODE=true`):
  `verify-rendered-revision.mjs` contrast report went from **26 findings** (12 text artifacts
  plus 14 duplicate ring findings) to **0 findings, pass: true**. Only the local SEO gate
  remains, which the workflow converts to a noindex diagnostic preview.
- A/B on the same dist: baseline reproduces all twelve production text failures exactly; the
  fixed scripts produce none, and the ring count is unchanged until the `--ll-focus` fix.
- `tests/rendered-contrast-pixel.test.ts`: two new browser tests fail on baseline
  (`fail` instead of `pass`) and pass with the fix.
- `tests/color-contrast.test.ts`: new focus-ring band test.
- Differential fuzz of `analyzePixelBackdrop` against `origin/main` with no inset: 300/300
  identical ratios and provable windows, so the change is inert unless an inset is supplied.
- 70 tests pass across the contrast, palette and homepage suites; `npm run check` reports 0
  errors and 0 warnings.

## 2026-11-13T23:20Z The plate scoped the wrong pixels entirely; manage the corrections budget

Run `43514656574` at `4890fb44` re-authored intake 146 and the fresh candidate reported **185
failure lines** (174 contrast, 8 rendered-reference, 3 layout), not the 21 from before. The
evidence showed the deeper cause:

- Eyebrow captions read 1.83 and 2.88 where the true values are 4.51 and 8.46. The kicker draws
  a 24x1px accent rule in a `::before` beside the label. The element-box plate sampled that rule
  as if it were behind the text. A whole-element plate also contains a border in the text colour,
  a rounded corner's unpainted wedge, and a one-pixel sliver outside the element at a fractional
  clip edge.
- So the edge-only inset from the previous commit was too narrow. The plate must be the surface
  behind the glyphs, nothing else.

### Fix

`paintedPixelMask` compares the capture with the paint intact and hidden, marks the pixels the
text or icon actually covered, and erodes one pixel so antialiased fringes cannot drag the ratio
down. `analyzePixelBackdrop` measures only masked pixels (band scope is unchanged for focus
rings). A 1px clip edge is excluded even when masked. If the visible capture is missing or the
mask covers too few pixels, the edge-inset plate is the fallback, and the full plate is the last
resort, so the change cannot invent a finding.

`scripts/bounded-corrections.mjs` now owns the managed-corrections markers and strip logic.
`contrast-sweep.mjs` re-exports them, and `production-experience-author.mjs` strips corrections
before applying the 80,000-character repairable-source limit. That limit exists to bound what a
repair model must rewrite; counting machine-generated corrections rejected a **24,837-character
authored stylesheet** because a render pass had appended **68,130 characters** of corrections to
a file that had 1,764 findings. Promotion of that candidate now succeeds.

### Verification

- Real built page of the fresh failing candidate: contrast findings went from 185 failure lines
  (1,764 non-pass targets) to **18, all `unresolved` and advisory, zero failures**. The caption
  targets now resolve against their real surfaces (`#808682` on `#14201d` = 4.51, `#454947` on
  `#f8f6f0` = 8.46) instead of the accent rule.
- `promote-creative-candidate.mjs` now accepts that candidate, which previously threw the
  repairable-source error.
- 365 tests pass across the contrast, palette, evidence-cache, repair-loop, author and homepage
  suites; `npm run check` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.

### Still open

- The evidence cache key does not include the measurement code, so a cached render can survive a
  gate fix. This run rendered fresh because the template copy changed the shared digest, but a
  pure gate change would be masked by the cache. Follow-up: add the gate/toolchain digest.
- The preview for this run was delivered through the pack fallback:
  `https://review-initial.launchloom-146-coastal-brush-painting-c.pages.dev`.

## 2026-11-13T23:40Z Cached evidence outlived the gate fix

The rendered-evidence cache key covered the client site, the candidate sources, the render
settings and the judge model, but not the measurement code, which lives in this repository
outside the client root. A contrast fix therefore changed every verdict without changing a single
input file, and a cached render could replay the old failures. `computeToolchainDigest` hashes the
`scripts/*.mjs` toolchain and joins the render key, so any gate change invalidates the evidence
it produced.

## 2026-11-16T18:40Z Repairs were being asked to rewrite 68k of machine CSS

The private rejection evidence answered why intake 146's repair never applied:

- round 00: `Reference-safe source validation failed for route-01: Required sealed token
  content.hero.image does not flow into output.`
- round 02: `<css input>:273:23: Missed semicolon`

Both are model output defects, and the payload explains them. `defaultRepairCandidate` read
`styles.css` from disk, which after a contrast pass contains the managed corrections block. For
this candidate that was **24,837 authored characters plus 68,130 characters of corrections**, all
sent to the model with an instruction to return a complete replacement. The model truncated and
mangled it.

`defaultRepairCandidate` now strips managed corrections from every file before the request. They
are a deterministic product of the last render and are regenerated after the repair, so the model
only ever sees authored source. This also removes a false rejection: the palette guard compared
the model's authored output against a baseline that contained correction-only colours.

Verified red then green on a new test that captures the outbound request body. 293 tests pass
across the repair, loop and author suites; `npm run check` is clean.

## 2026-11-16T19:05Z The pack inner-hero links were losing to cascade layers

The pack fallback's `/services/` hero measured three genuine failures: `#027262` "Home" on
`#10211f` at 2.847:1, "Explore services" at 3.387:1 on its own `#7cd5c1` fill, and the phone link
at 2.847:1.

Cause: `site.css` is bundled inside `@layer legacy-site`, while `experience-packs.css` is
unlayered. An unlayered rule always beats a layered one **regardless of specificity**, so the
pack's `a { color: var(--ll-link, #027262) }` won over `.recipe-local-trades .breadcrumb` and
`.recipe-local-trades .cta`. Adding `!important` or a more specific selector inside the layered
sheet cannot fix it.

The pairings now live in the unlayered inline `colorRoles` block in `SiteLayout.astro`, alongside
the existing `.split-section` focus rule. Rebuilt the pack site and re-probed: breadcrumb
`#bac9c4` on `#10211f` (6.6:1), CTA `#000000` on `#7cd5c1` (12:1), phone link `#ffffff` (15.9:1).

Open: the same pack page still reports `text paint is indistinguishable` at 1.000 for the service
card labels. That is the hide-did-not-take family, not the cascade. It needs its own evidence pass;
the Playwright browser binary was replaced mid-session (`chromium_headless_shell-1243` missing),
so the browser probes could not continue.

## 2026-11-16T19:30Z The analyzer's 128k reservation is what OpenRouter refused

Run `43936268157` did not reach authoring either:
`Reference analyzer failed for route-01 (402): This request requires more credits, or fewer
max_tokens. You requested up to 128000 tokens, but can only afford 8039.`

That 128k cap is this workstream's own change from earlier: 9000 was too small because DeepSeek
spends hidden reasoning against the same budget, so it was raised to the Go transport's ceiling.
OpenRouter prices the whole reservation, and the key holds `limit_remaining = 1.685` of a $2
limit, so a 128k reservation is refused outright.

The OpenRouter analyzer now reserves 32,000 tokens, four times the budget that starved the JSON
and a quarter of the refused reservation, overridable with `REFERENCE_ANALYZER_MAX_TOKENS`.
17 analyzer tests pass.

## 2026-11-16T19:55Z The pack preview died on a five-second reload

Run `43940456447` (pack renderer, `pack_id=bold-utility`) got all the way through the build and the
contrast audit, then failed the rendered revision check with
`/services/ tablet: browser: page.reload: Timeout 5000ms exceeded`.

`verifyApprovedRoutes` gives every page action a 5,000 ms default, which is right for selector
assertions and wrong for a `networkidle` navigation on an image-heavy page. The initial load,
refresh and reduced-motion reload now get 30,000 ms; element assertions keep the short budget.
That is a gate-robustness fix, not a design change: the check still fails if the page does not
come back.

## 2026-11-16T20:20Z Generation is blocked on provider credit, not code

Three consecutive dispatches failed before producing anything, each further upstream:

Code state is otherwise the best it has been: the pack build audits **0 contrast findings** on
